title: A pipeline pane named by a layout slot shows inside that slot's rect of the composed display, captured at the render graph's root, and publishes the mapping a display point maps through to the pane's pixel
binding: The positive leg boots an offscreen 64x64 world whose one layout slot fills the left half of the display with the pane instance, a one-pass graph that writes opaque magenta over its whole extent. Once the pane has installed and submitted frames, world.screenshot captures the composed display at the render graph's root: every pixel of the left half is magenta, and the right half, which no slot fills, is not. world.view.panes then reads the mapping the host published from the same placement: the pane instance's whole 32x64 image over the left half, a display point at (8.5, 40.5) picking the pane's pixel (8, 40) and a hit walk that ends on the pane, which renders from no camera, and a point on the right half picking nothing. The discriminating leg boots the same world with the slot moved to the right half, so the left-half observations turn red and the right-half ones turn green: the capture and the mapping both show where the slot places the pane, not only that a pane rendered.

expect.text: panes=1 | pane0 instance:pane pane 0,0 0.5x1 source 32x64 crop 0,0 32x64 layout Identity fit Stretch destination Presentation
